                    ### Question
                    A 28-year-old woman with a history of migraines presents to your office due to sudden loss of vision in her left eye and difficulty speaking. Two weeks ago she experienced muscle aches, fever, and cough. Her muscle aches are improving but she continues to have a cough. She also feels as though she has been more tired than usual. She had a similar episode of vision loss 2 years ago and had an MRI at that time. She has a family history of migraines and takes propranolol daily. On swinging light test there is decreased constriction of the left pupil relative to the right pupil. You repeat the MRI and note enhancing lesions in the left optic nerve. Which of the following is used to prevent progression of this condition?

opb. Methotrexate
opc. Natalizumab
opd. Infliximab
ope. Adalimumab

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms, including sudden vision loss and enhancing lesions on MRI, suggest optic neuritis, which is often associated with multiple sclerosis (MS). The presence of enhancing lesions in the optic nerve on MRI supports the diagnosis of MS. Natalizumab is a monoclonal antibody used to prevent the progression of MS by inhibiting the migration of immune cells into the central nervous system, thereby reducing inflammation and the frequency of relapses. The retrieved evidence paths confirm the association between MRI findings and the use of natalizumab in managing MS. Other options like dexamethasone, methotrexate, infliximab, and adalimumab are not standard treatments for preventing MS progression. Therefore, natalizumab is the most appropriate choice for preventing the progression of this condition.
